challenges.title: Counting matches
challenges.description: boot.log contains 3 lines with ERROR; one of those lines contains ERROR twice.
hints: -c counts lines, not occurrences.
Use grep -o ... | wc -l to count occurrences.
challenges.explanation:
grep -c prints the number of matching lines, so a line with two matches still counts once. To count every
       occurrence, use grep -o "ERROR" boot.log | wc -l.
challenges.source: Linux, Bash & Embedded Debugging Handbook · Text processing with grep
options: Nothing; -c only sets the exit code

challenges.title: Reading octal permissions
challenges.description: A diagnostic script is installed with chmod 754 collect.sh.
challenges.instructions: Type the 9-character permission string (as shown by ls -l, without the leading file-type character).
hints: Each digit is read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).
Digits are owner, group, others.
challenges.explanation:
7 = 4+2+1 = rwx for the owner, 5 = 4+1 = r-x for the group, 4 = r-- for others. Others can read the script
            but not execute it.
challenges.source: Linux, Bash & Embedded Debugging Handbook · Ch. 3 Users, Groups and Permissions

challenges.title: Follow a service's journal
challenges.description: bmcweb is restarting during a Redfish test and you want to watch its log live.
challenges.instructions: Fill the blank so journalctl keeps printing new entries for the unit.
hints: Same letter as tail's live option.
There is a long form too.
challenges.explanation:
journalctl -u UNIT limits output to one systemd unit and -f (--follow) keeps streaming new entries, like
         tail -f. Add --since "10 min ago" to start from a recent point.
challenges.source: Linux, Bash & Embedded Debugging Handbook · systemd & journald

challenges.title: Exit status
challenges.description: A Bash wrapper runs a command and then checks $?.
hints: Non-zero exit codes signal failure.
Automation should check this after every critical step.
challenges.explanation:
$? holds the exit status of the last command: 0 means success, anything else is a failure code. set -e makes
       a script stop at the first failing command.
challenges.source: Linux, Bash & Embedded Debugging Handbook · Bash automation
options: The previous command ran for 0 seconds

challenges.title: The dangerous cleanup
challenges.description: A log-rotation script runs as root on a lab controller.
challenges.instructions: What is the most serious problem?
hints: What does the command expand to when get_log_dir prints nothing?
Bash can abort on empty variables.
challenges.explanation:
An empty or unset variable turns the command into rm -rf /*. Use rm -rf -- "${LOG_DIR:?LOG_DIR is empty}"/*
        so the script aborts instead, and add set -euo pipefail at the top.
challenges.source: Linux, Bash & Embedded Debugging Handbook · Bash safety; safety labels
options: If LOG_DIR is empty, the command becomes rm -rf /* ; quote it and guard with ${LOG_DIR:?}
Command substitution is not allowed in assignments

challenges.title: fetch versus pull
challenges.description: You want to see what teammates pushed without changing your working branch.
hints: One command only downloads.
The other downloads and merges.
challenges.explanation:
git fetch updates remote-tracking branches such as origin/main without touching your branch or files.
       git pull is fetch followed by merge (or rebase) into the current branch.
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 1 Git Fundamentals

challenges.title: Feature branch workflow
challenges.description: You are adding UART retry logic to the shared test framework.
challenges.instructions: Order the steps of a standard feature-branch workflow.
hints: Create the branch before you change anything.
A pull request needs the branch on the remote.
challenges.explanation:
Branch first so main stays clean, commit your staged work, push the branch with -u to set its upstream,
            then open a pull request so CI and reviewers check the change before it merges.
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 3 Professional Git Workflows
steps: Edit the files and stage them with git add
Open a pull request for review

challenges.title: Undo the last commit
challenges.description: You committed too early and want to undo the last commit but keep its changes staged.
hints: Three modes: one keeps the index, one keeps only files, one discards everything.
You want to keep the most.
challenges.explanation:
--soft moves the branch pointer back and leaves the changes staged. --mixed (the default) unstages them;
         --hard discards them. Only reset commits you have not pushed.
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 5 Git Troubleshooting

challenges.title: A leaked password
challenges.description: You pushed a commit containing a BMC admin password to a shared repository.
hints: Clones and forks may already have the commit.
History rewriting cannot recall copies.
challenges.explanation:
Once pushed, assume the secret is compromised: change it immediately. Then purge it from history (for
       example with git filter-repo), and prevent recurrences with credentials stores and pre-commit scanning.
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 5 Git Troubleshooting and Security
options: Force-push and assume nobody saw it
Delete the file in a new commit; that is enough
Rotate (change) the password, then remove it from history and add secret scanning

challenges.title: Hunting a regression
challenges.description: A test passed at tag v2.13 and fails at HEAD, 300 commits later.
challenges.instructions: Which Git feature finds the first failing commit most efficiently?
hints: About log2(300) ≈ 9 test runs.
It performs a binary search over history.
challenges.explanation:
git bisect binary-searches between a good and a bad commit; git bisect run can even execute the test
       automatically at each step. blame shows who last changed each line, which is a different question.
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 5 Git Troubleshooting
